name: גִּדַּלְתִּי
gloss: I have magnified; I have brought up
summary: Giddalti son of Heman, one of David's singers, who drew the twenty-second lot (1Ch 25:4, 29). The name is the piel perfect, first person, of גָּדַל: “I have magnified” or “I have brought up”. It stands beside his brother's name Romamti-ezer, “I have exalted (רוֹמַמְתִּי) help”, and the two verbs are scripture's own pair: of bringing up children, בָּנִים גִּדַּלְתִּי וְרוֹמַמְתִּי (Isa 1:2; also Isa 23:4), and of praise, “magnify (גַּדְּלוּ) Yahweh with me, and let us exalt (וּנְרוֹמְמָה) his name together” (Psa 34:4).

evidence.note: The sons of Heman: … אֱלִיאָתָה גִדַּלְתִּי וְרֹמַמְתִּי עֶזֶר …
“The twenty-second, לְגִדַּלְתִּי, his sons and his brothers, twelve.”
“בָּנִים גִּדַּלְתִּי וְרוֹמַמְתִּי”: the same two verbs, the same form.
“I have not brought up (גִדַּלְתִּי) young men nor raised (רוֹמַמְתִּי) virgins.”

note: BDB's c.aq.ak also counts Isa 23:4, the piel verb. Whether the sense is “I have magnified (God)”, as fits a singer, or “I have brought up”, scripture does not say.
